# Using AI tools to contribute

AI tools can help you write code, tests and docs, and you're welcome to use them. What we care about is that a person who understands the change stands behind it, because every pull request costs a maintainer time to review.

## You own your contribution

Anything submitted from your account is your responsibility, whether or not AI helped. Before you open a pull request:

- read every line of it
- run it, and test it on a real panel where it makes sense
- make sure you can explain how it works and why it's right
- check it follows [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)

"The AI wrote it" isn't an answer in review.

## Be upfront

If AI wrote a large part of a pull request, say so in the description. It doesn't count against you. It helps the reviewer know what to look at.

## Don't flood us

- No pull requests or issues opened by an agent running on its own. A person has to open and own them.
- No more than 3 open pull requests at a time.
- Keep changes small and focused.
- Don't post AI-written replies in reviews, issues or discussions without reading and editing them yourself.

## Same standards

AI-assisted work gets the same review as any other. Maintainers may close, without a detailed review, pull requests and issues that look generated and unchecked: changes that don't build, don't match the issue, invent APIs, or add a lot of code for little reason. Repeated low-effort submissions can get an account blocked from the repo.
